title: UPDATE: Jev Grabs 1 Percentage Point of AI Market in One Month
summary:
Corporate spending on artificial intelligence is splitting between the adoption of budget models and high cost generative tools. Data from Ramp shows that new, cheaper models and routers are driving costs down, with the provider Jev capturing 1 percentage point of market adoption in a single month. Simultaneously, the increased use of expensive image and video generation models from vendors such as Higgsfield and Runway is pushing expenditures upward.

This spending divergence follows a surge in provider turnover, where nearly 8% of firms switched their primary AI model in September. The switching rate, a three month moving average, is driven by a rapid cycle of new model releases and price cuts from OpenAI. These trends are stripping pricing power from AI labs as services become commoditized, which analysts suggest will lead to falling prices and margins for AI companies.

We clearly see AI spend pulled in two different directions.

On the downside, new and cheaper models are pushing AI spend down. Jev captured an entire percentage point of market adoption within a month (unheard of growth). And routers continue to gain.

On the upside, the increased adoption of expensive image and video generation models will push AI spend up, like Higgsfield and Runway.

selectedTweets.text:
Firms are switching AI providers at the highest rate Ramp has seen.

The monthly share of businesses switching their top model provider reached nearly 8% in September, measured as a three-month moving average. 

We last saw comparable switching when Anthropic launched Opus 4 and Sonnet 4 in May 2025.

Rapid model releases and OpenAI’s price cuts are giving firms reasons to switch. The more willing and able firms are to switch, the less pricing power AI labs have.

Another sign that AI models may be becoming commodities.

Read more at our data blog: https://t.co/SLDWlsyGEe
